mechanism_conclusion.lazy_release: A durable reservation-level CANCELLED tombstone can logically revoke the old reservation before every cell is physically cleaned. A new claimant follows the stale cell's holder reservation ID, verifies current CANCELLED, then CAS-reclaims that cell under its deterministic reservation ID. Its partial reclaim prefix remains PREPARED and non-authoritative.
mechanism_conclusion.cleanup_not_authority: Best-effort cell release is garbage collection, not the revocation proof. Requiring all cell rows to be cleaned first causes avoidable false exclusion after crash/rate-limit interruption.
mechanism_conclusion.tombstone_missing: Missing cancellation evidence must fail closed. Treating missing as dead/free is unsafe when stale holder rows remain.
mechanism_conclusion.incarnation: Cell delete/recreate requires current blob/incarnation-sensitive identity; logical name or a resettable numeric epoch is an ABA hole.
mechanism_conclusion.rollback: If the repository authority itself is rolled back from CANCELLED to an old GRANTED view and no independent monotonic witness survives, the model cannot distinguish the rollback; late-old behavior is unsafe. This remains an anti-rollback unresolved child, not an accepted route.

phase1_assessment.repository_local_lazy_release: Chat-capable with lightweight repository CAS/readback; no hosted coordinator, hosted compute/storage allowance, paid/trial/monthly credit, manual user execution, or incremental monetary cost is required for the tested scope.
phase1_assessment.residual_richer_mode_or_manual_user_exec: none for tested repository-local lazy release
unresolved_children: authority-domain rollback/restore that erases the durable CANCELLED witness

scope_limit: Three logical cells, six claim shapes, none/partial/full cleanup, current/missing/rolled-back tombstone, cell ABA and incarnation identity. Repository-wide rollback is modeled as an explicit negative control.
exact_continuation: Cancellation tombstone retention/compaction under repository-only zero-quota constraints. Compare permanent per-reservation tombstone, compact monotonic per-cell retired-holder floor, append-only reservation terminal index, generation-level cancellation watermark, and fail-closed no-GC. Enumerate all cells cleaned, stale-cell restore, cell delete/recreate, task-key reuse, repository branch rewind/restore, response loss, and rate-limit interruption. Determine the weakest durable witness that permits bounded state growth without allowing a cancelled reservation to become authoritative again; explicitly test whether any witness in the same rollback domain can solve a complete repository rewind, or whether that case is information-theoretically indistinguishable and must remain unresolved.
